Day 22 of 100 · AWS Networking Foundations

AWS CDK

#100DaysOfCloudAndSecurityAWS Networking FoundationsTopic verified by artifact

The AWS CDK lets infrastructure be modeled with programming-language constructs and synthesized into CloudFormation.

Architecture / mental model

CDK app → constructs → cdk synth → CloudFormation template → stack

How it works

CDK constructs package infrastructure patterns at different abstraction levels. The code is not a replacement for CloudFormation underneath; synthesis produces a CloudFormation template that becomes the deployment contract.

Using a programming language gives functions, loops, types and reusable modules, but abstraction can hide important defaults. `cdk diff` brings generated infrastructure change back into view before deployment.

The durable skill is understanding the AWS resources being generated, not merely learning a fluent API that can produce them.

Hands-on reference

cdk synth
cdk diff
cdk deploy

Verification

Inspect synthesized template and diff before deployment, then confirm the resulting CloudFormation stack/resources match intended design.

Field note / gotcha

High-level constructs can create more resources or permissions than the few lines of CDK code suggest. Review synthesized output when security or cost boundaries matter.

Security considerations

Treat construct defaults as inputs to review, not automatic best practice. Examine generated IAM policies, network exposure and removal policies.

What I learned

Abstraction is useful when you can still see through it.
